text:
Before the drain dispatches a job, check whether any work item has a queued fix job that has not yet been read (only request.json in its job folder). Look at items whose failure class matches the job's likely class, or whose cause is a check every job runs, such as a test that rejects unrelated jobs. When one does, run that fix job first, or hold the exposed job and print a drain line naming the blocking fix job. Today, after fix jobs 20261112-005306-pa2j (the drain test that does not finish its shard) and 20261112-110546-n4x6 (status measures with no real-records run) were queued, jobs 20261030-033234-vm1m, 20261030-033225-g36k and 20261112-180947-td6x were still dispatched and rejected for those same causes. Acceptance: (1) A drain test with a queued, unread fix job for a check every job runs dispatches the fix job before other improvement-turn items. (2) A drain test where a job's class matches an open fix item's class holds the job and prints the blocking fix job id. (3) Jobs with no matching open fix are dispatched as before. (4) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass. (5) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: The drain keeps sending jobs into a failure whose queued fix job has not run, so the same known fault keeps rejecting new jobs
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass

Files: request.json, CHANGELOG.md
